display.purpose: Stat-card numbers, the single largest figures on a dashboard view.

headline.purpose: The top-bar page title on every screen.

body.purpose: Running text and table content; the unweighted default.

label.purpose: Uppercase section eyebrows, table column headers, form section titles.

shadows.name: panel
shadows.purpose: The sidebar and main content panel, directly against the gradient backdrop. Deepest ambient shadow in the system.

shadows.name: sm
shadows.purpose: Resting state for cards, stat cards, inputs, chips.

shadows.name: md
shadows.purpose: Hover/focus response only (stat card hover, calendar event hover/focus-visible) — never a resting shadow.

shadows.name: lg
shadows.purpose: Overlays: modals, toasts, the open mobile sidebar drawer, the mobile bottom nav.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Button/icon-button scale(.97) on :active — the system's universal press feedback.

motion.name: toast-in
motion.purpose: Toast entrance: slides in from the right, fades in.

motion.name: toast-out
motion.purpose: Toast exit — deliberately faster than its entrance.

motion.name: modal-open
motion.purpose: Modal scale-up + translateY entrance from the backdrop show state.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The only solid-fill, full-pill call to action in the system.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; gap:8px; padding:10px 20px; border-radius:999px; font-size:14px; font-weight:700; border:1px solid transparent; cursor:pointer; background:#1d6bf3; color:#fff; box-shadow:0 6px 14px rgba(29,107,243,.24); transition:background .15s, box-shadow .15s, transform .16s cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background:#1558cc; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform:scale(.97); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline:2px solid #4a8cf7; outline-offset:2px; }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Secondary action — cancel, dismiss, or any action that shouldn't compete with the primary one.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; gap:8px; padding:10px 20px; border-radius:999px; font-size:14px; font-weight:700; cursor:pointer; background:#fff; border:1px solid #e4eaf4; color:#2b3a55; transition:background .15s, border-color .15s, transform .16s cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1); } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background:#f6f9fd; border-color:#cdd6e4; } .ds-btn-outline:active { transform:scale(.97); }

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: Light tint + dark text pill, never a solid fill — the visual tell that separates a status badge from a button. Four color variants shown; Present is the example instance.
components.html: Present
components.css: .ds-badge { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:5px; padding:4px 12px; border-radius:999px; font-size:12.5px; font-weight:700; } .ds-badge-present { background:#dcf6e6; color:#15803d; } .ds-badge-late { background:#ffefd9; color:#b45309; } .ds-badge-absent { background:#fde4e4; color:#b91c1c; } .ds-badge-excused { background:#e0e7ff; color:#4338ca; }

components.name: Card
components.description: The base container for every grouped section of content.
components.html:
Today's Classes

Card content goes here.
components.css: .ds-card { background:#fff; border-radius:20px; border:1px solid #e8eef7; box-shadow:0 1px 2px rgba(30,64,120,.05); } .ds-card-header { display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:space-between; gap:12px; padding:20px 24px 4px; } .ds-card-header h3 { margin:0; font-size:16px; font-weight:800; letter-spacing:-.01em; color:#0e1a33; } .ds-card-body { padding:16px 24px 24px; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Standard text field with the system's signature 3px soft-blue focus glow.
components.html: <input class="ds-input" type="text" placeholder="Search name, ID, email...">
components.css: .ds-input { width:100%; padding:10px 14px; border:1px solid #e4eaf4; border-radius:12px; font-size:14px; color:#0e1a33; background:#fff; transition:border-color .15s, box-shadow .15s; } .ds-input::placeholder { color:#55637a; } .ds-input:focus { outline:none; border-color:#4a8cf7; box-shadow:0 0 0 3px #dce9ff; }

components.name: Sidebar Nav Link
components.description: Active state is a solid accent fill with a colored glow — not a tint or a border — so current location is unmissable.
components.html: Dashboard
components.css: .ds-nav-link { display:flex; align-items:center; gap:12px; padding:10px 14px; border-radius:999px; color:#3d4b63; font-size:13.5px; font-weight:600; transition:background .15s, color .15s, box-shadow .15s; } .ds-nav-link:hover { background:#f6f9fd; color:#0e1a33; } .ds-nav-link-active { background:#1d6bf3; color:#fff; box-shadow:0 8px 18px rgba(29,107,243,.30); }

components.name: Toast
components.description: A colored left border is the only status signal; the toast body itself never changes background color.
components.html: Saved successfully.
components.css: .ds-toast { min-width:280px; max-width:360px; background:#fff; border-radius:16px; box-shadow:0 18px 48px rgba(30,64,120,.18); padding:14px 16px; display:flex; align-items:flex-start; gap:10px; border-left:4px solid #1d6bf3; } .ds-toast-success { border-color:#16a34a; } .ds-toast-msg { font-size:13.5px; color:#14213d; flex:1; }

components.name: Modal
components.description: Conceptually a panel over the panel — shares the 24px radius scale with the sidebar and main content panel.
components.css: .ds-modal { background:#fff; border-radius:24px; width:100%; max-width:520px; box-shadow:0 18px 48px rgba(30,64,120,.18); } .ds-modal-header { display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:space-between; padding:20px 24px; border-bottom:1px solid #e8eef7; } .ds-modal-header h3 { margin:0; font-size:17px; font-weight:800; letter-spacing:-.01em; color:#0e1a33; } .ds-modal-body { padding:22px 24px; } .ds-modal-footer { padding:16px 24px; border-top:1px solid #e8eef7; display:flex; justify-content:flex-end; gap:10px; }

narrative.overview:
This is a system whose entire purpose is catching attendance fraud, and it deliberately does not look or feel like one. Instead of alarms, locks, or heavy institutional chrome, it uses a soft blue gradient backdrop with two floating white panels — the sidebar and the main content panel — riding above it like paper on a desk. Verification happens quietly and constantly underneath (GPS radius, device binding, signed QR payloads, server-side re-checks on every rule), but the surface stays calm, precise, and trustworthy. The product earns trust by being legible and unhurried, not by looking locked down.

Every interactive surface is a pill or a rounded rectangle; nothing is sharp-cornered. One accent color — Gatekeeper Blue — marks everything selected or actionable; it never competes with the four status colors (Present, Late, Absent, Excused), which are reserved strictly for attendance state. The whole system reads as soft-edged and quietly confident: generous radii, restrained shadows, bold (800-weight) headings doing hierarchy's work instead of loud color or large size jumps, and a scale(.97) press on every button that makes the interface feel like it's listening.
keyCharacteristics: Floating-panel shell: a visible gradient backdrop behind two elevated white (or dark-surface) panels, never a single flat background
One brand accent (Gatekeeper Blue), four status colors that never do double duty as decoration
Pills everywhere interactive; cards and panels round at a larger, consistent scale
Headings differentiate by weight (800) and negative letter-spacing, not by dramatic size jumps
Full light/dark theme parity — every token has a dark-mode counterpart, not just an inverted background

rules.name: The Single Accent Rule
rules.body: Gatekeeper Blue is the only brand color. Every other hue on screen is either a neutral (slate) or a status signal — never a second decorative accent.

rules.name: The Status Colors Never Multitask Rule
rules.body: Present green, Late amber, Absent red, and Excused violet map 1:1 to attendance meaning everywhere in the product. They are never repurposed for unrelated success/warning/error messaging elsewhere.

rules.name: The Weight-Over-Size Rule
rules.body: Headings jump straight to font-weight 800 rather than stepping through 500/600/700; the type scale stays compact because weight and negative tracking do the differentiation, not dramatic size jumps.

rules.name: The Panel Lift Rule
rules.body: Depth decreases as you move inward: backdrop (flat) → sidebar/main panel (Panel shadow) → cards (Small shadow) → nothing, until an element becomes an overlay (modal/toast) or gains interactive focus (Medium shadow), both of which jump back up.

rules.name: The Shape Rule
rules.body: Panels round at 24px, cards at 20px, inputs and small blocks at 12px; buttons, badges, chips, and tabs are always full pills. A new component picks from this exact scale — it never introduces its own radius value.

dos: Do use the pill shape (999px) for every button, badge, chip, and tab — it's the single most identifying shape in the system.
Do differentiate heading levels with weight (800) and negative letter-spacing before reaching for a bigger font size.
Do keep status colors (Present/Late/Absent/Excused) exclusive to attendance meaning; use slate neutrals for anything else that needs a "pending/inactive" look.
Do give the active sidebar item a solid accent fill with a glow shadow, not a subtle tint or border — navigation state should be unmissable.
Do make exits (toast dismiss, modal close) faster than entrances.
donts: Don't introduce a second brand accent color. Gatekeeper Blue is the only one; a new "secondary" color is almost certainly meant to be a status color or a slate neutral instead.
Don't give a card, panel, or button a radius outside the five-step scale (12/16/20/24/999).
Don't use a flat solid fill for a status badge — badges are always a light tint + dark text pair, never a saturated solid background (that's reserved for buttons).

Don't add drop shadows to small, flat UI like table rows or list items; the shadow vocabulary is reserved for panels, cards, and overlays — most of the interface stays flat against its parent surface.
Don't reach for a second typeface. Plus Jakarta Sans at a higher weight is the answer to "this needs to stand out more," not a new font.
